$pluginRootComment: Cursor does not document a plugin-root variable. The fallback MUST stay byte-identical to the symlink target in `.install` below (~/.cursor/plugins/local/<name>) — that is the only path a local install actually creates. The two diverging is not a cosmetic bug: the generated hooks.json sets failClosed:true, so if CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset and this expression resolves to a path with no confirm-mutation.sh in it, Cursor fails the hook closed and blocks EVERY shell command, not just the guarded ones. Every script in core/lib is also self-locating, so this expression is a convenience rather than the correctness mechanism — but the hook command line is resolved by Cursor, not by the script, so it gets no such safety net.

manifest.$comment: Cursor's published plugin schema (cursor/plugins schemas/plugin.schema.json) is additionalProperties:false and its author object permits name and email only — `url` is rejected. Nothing is lost: `homepage` and `repository` are both permitted top-level keys and already carry it. All 13 plugins in cursor/plugins use exactly {name, email}. Cursor's runtime loader ignores the extra key, which is why a local install looks fine; the publication schema its own CI enforces does not. Same lenient-loader/strict-validator split as Codex, different surface.

mcp.$comment: Cursor discovers mcp.json at the plugin root automatically — no manifest key. Written in the standard {"mcpServers": {...}} shape, same as every other mcp.json a user has ever pasted.

hooks.$comment: Different event name, different payload, different denial protocol (stdout {"permission":"deny"} + exit 2). The only host needing its own dialect.

marketplace.$comment: Multi-plugin repos need .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json. Listing on cursor.com/marketplace is human-reviewed and requires the repo to be public — this host is NOT on our release cadence.
marketplace.$flavourComment: cursor/plugins schemas/marketplace.schema.json is additionalProperties:false at every level and differs from the default shape three ways: the marketplace description lives under `metadata`, not at the top level; `owner` permits name and email only; and a plugin entry permits name/source/description/minClientVersions only — no `version`, no `author`. The plugin's own manifest is where its version and author belong, and duplicating them in the index is what the schema is refusing. cursor/plugins' own .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json is exactly this shape.
